sources.entry: Galene - Video conferencing server that is easy to deploy and that requires moderate server resources. (Source Code) MIT Go

summary.one_liner: Galene is a self-hostable videoconferencing server written in Go, designed to be easy to deploy and to need only moderate server resources.
summary.what_it_does: Galene is a videoconferencing system that the README describes as fully featured, easy to deploy, and light on server resources. The quick start builds a single Go binary with CGO disabled, creates a groups directory, and writes a JSON group file that defines users, passwords and permissions (for example "op" for operator). After starting the ./galene process, users open the server in a browser and log in with a configured username and password. The README points to separate documents covering full installation, usage and administration, writing clients, the client protocol, and an administrative API. Contribution is through the project's mailing list or GitHub pull requests, and the author asks that general discussion happen on the mailing list rather than GitHub.
use_cases: running a video meeting server for a small group
hosting video calls on modest hardware
setting up group-based video rooms with user permissions
building a custom videoconferencing client against a server protocol
stack: JavaScript (browser client, implied by client documentation)
notable: Single Go binary built with a plain go build command and CGO disabled
Groups defined as JSON files with per-user passwords and permissions
Separate documentation for installation, administration, client writing, protocol, and admin API
Designed to require moderate server resources
caveats: Quick start serves a self-signed certificate, so browsers show an unknown certificate warning
The quick start uses a sample demo account with a weak password that must be changed for real use
Full installation details are in a separate document (galene-install.md), not in this README
keywords: run video chat on my server
